//: Shared by qute-literal.test.ts (the Manager's escape) and OperatorPromptQuteCorpusTest (EDDI's real Qute engine, Java). The rule is conservative: every `{` outside the Manager's own context block, an existing {|...|} block and a ${vault|eddivault|vars|connection|caller:...} mention is wrapped in its own unparsed block ({|{|}); a run of backslashes before a brace goes inside the block. kind: expression = the engine, made to parse the text, changes or rejects it; inert = the engine leaves it as written (escaped anyway, so no rule has to know why); mention = contains a reference mention, which the escape splits around and LlmTask wraps itself; raw = an unparsed block the author wrote, kept; live = contains the context block, which stays evaluated. For every kind the engine must render `escaped` back to exactly `text` (live: apart from the context block, which is evaluated). Add a case here before changing the rule; the Java test will say if the engine disagrees.
